text:
Ava: heads-up — ran a degraded-region sim this morning. when us-west-2 CPU baseline hit ~90% we triggered auto-swap and saw read fanout to global replicas spike latency ~3x. need to decide tenant swap prioritization and ordering. thoughts?
Rajat: can you paste the relevant logs/commands?
Ava: snippet below — the swap started automatically after operator threshold hit. see the cache miss/replica-fanout pattern: ```
[1728888889] swap-start tenant=acct-309 priority=auto reason=region-degraded
[1728888890] read-fanout tenant=acct-309 -> replicas 4,7,2 latency_ms=320
[1728888891] cache-primed tenant=acct-309 prewarm=false
```
Ava: example operator kick: `curl -X POST /controlplane/v1/tenants/acct-309/swap -d '{"target":"us-east-1","mode":"staged"}'`
Marta: high-level: we should score tenants by (data-residency, write-qps, sla-tier, kms-bound). suggested sort: non-resident & low-write first, tolerant tiers next, then resident-with-consent, resident-without-consent never auto-swap.
Leo: +1 on scoring. important: resident-without-consent can't ever be moved across jurisdiction boundaries. for those we should serve degraded read-only proxies in-region and surface clear 429/503 semantics to callers.
Rajat: operational concern: if we kick too many swaps concurrently we create a KV cache storm and a burst of model loads. we need bounded concurrency (default 3-5 tenants simultaneously) and a cool-down window between batches. also pre-warm reads before cutover.
Ava: proposal (short):
- priority order: non-resident low-write -> non-resident high-write -> tolerant SLAs -> resident-with-consent -> resident-without-consent (manual)
- concurrency: 5 (configurable per-region)
- batch cooldown: 60s
- prewarm: yes, with `prime_read_cache=true` flag
- telemetry: tag swaps with `swap.reason`, `swap.plan`, `swap.batch_id`
Rajat: API shape needs to support this: `/v1/tenants/{id}/swap?dry_run=true&prime_read_cache=true&batch_id=...` and a bulk endpoint `/v1/swap-batches` that accepts ordered tenant lists and concurrency/cooldown knobs. we should include an abort endpoint too.
Marta: scoring nuance: KMS-bound tenants should get a +penalty because key rewrap/replication adds N secs. also flag tenants with PII labels to avoid automatic movement unless legal-approved.
Leo: add a runtime safety valve: abort if region error rate > 10% or if model-load OOMs > 2 in last 5m. include operator-visible runbook step to revert partial swaps.
ops-bot: :rotating_light: automated-swap triggered for region us-west-2 at 1728888889 (batch_id=bn-1728888)
Ava: i'll draft an RFC follow-up and a short ops-runbook snippet. putting a tiny runbook draft here: ```
operator steps:
1) dry-run: POST /v1/swap-batches {tenants: [..], concurrency: 5, cooldown: 60, dry_run: true}
2) inspect telemetry `swap.batch_id` and wait 2m
3) kick real batch with prime_read_cache=true
4) monitor `swap.progress` and abort if error_rate>0.1 or model_load_failures>2
```
Marta: can you also add a small test harness to simulate KMS latency and resident flags? that made a huge diff in the sim.
Ava: will add tests + a couple of dashboards (swap L7 failures, cache-miss ratio, prewarm latency). will share RFC link once ready. :shipit:
Rajat: :thumbsup: happy to review the API surface.
Leo: :thinking_face: consider defaulting non-resident tenants to opt-in for auto-swap in case app owners rely on regional placement for latency-sensitive features. we should document impact in console.
Ava: agree — will add an opt-out toggle per-tenant and surface a warning with estimated added p50/p95 latency.
Marta: ok — thanks all, this should keep busy from the eviction/hand-off churn we've seen.
